profile.what: CrowdStrike sells cloud-based security software that protects laptops, servers and cloud workloads from attack. Its Falcon platform runs through a single small program on each device.
profile.money: Customers pay annual subscriptions per device and per module, and tend to add modules over time. A faulty software update in 2024 caused a worldwide computer outage and tested customer loyalty.
profile.valued: CrowdStrike is valued on a multiple of sales and on recurring-revenue growth, because reported earnings are still close to zero. Its high valuation depends on growth continuing and on stock-based pay falling as a share of revenue.

summary.sentence: A fast-growing security software leader that has yet to earn a steady reported profit.
strengths: Revenue has grown every year in the record.
Free cash flow is positive and rising.

meaning.what_it_does: Sells cloud-based software that protects computers and servers from attack.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Annual subscriptions, priced per device and per module.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: One lightweight agent on each device lets customers add modules without new installs.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: Another faulty update like its 2024 outage, or Microsoft's bundled security wins on price.

moat.summary: Threat data from millions of devices improves detection, but Microsoft and others compete hard.

industry.summary: Attackers and defences change constantly, so a security vendor must keep its products ahead every year.

management.summary: Founder-led and fast-growing, but still loss-making on reported earnings because of heavy stock-based pay.

financial_health.ratio_gaps: Not available from the data source, so not shown: a ten-year record, inventory and receivables turnover, the quick ratio, goodwill and tangible book value, and maintenance capex split from growth capex. Owner earnings therefore deduct all capex, which is conservative.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of the one method that applies: (1) Owner cash flow: $303M a year: free cash flow less stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
